Hi Samir 2 0
4 quick tech notes based on the constraints you shared:

Auth and deployment:
- Dedicated: we support mTLS + customer-managed KMS for key material. For initial pilot, short-lived API tokens issued by your control plane (rotated) work well; we also support OAuth2 client credentials if you want token exchange.

SDK / RPC patterns:
- SDKs (Python/Node/Go) include both sync rank() and batch_rank() calls.
- For UI low-latency path: use rank(sync) with top_k tuned to the minimal acceptable k (we recommend starting at k=10 for live UI to keep latency down).
- For offline re-ranking jobs: use batch_rank() with sharded workers and streaming upload of candidate embeddings.

Structured output/tool calling:
- Our ranking API can return structured JSON fields (we provide field mappings). You can ask for additional fields to be returned (title, author, confidence_score) and we can include provenance metadata. That should integrate with your enrichment service.

Routing and fallbacks:
- Smart routing allows routing by latency vs cost. For Dedicated, set a policy to prefer dedicated pool and fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is saturated.

Performance notes:
- For top_k=10 on a 150-candidate pool we typically see median latency ~60-120ms on A100-class hosts with optimized kernels, P95 ~180ms; results vary by query length. We'll provide a staging endpoint you can hit from your infra to measure real numbers.

I'll attach a short sample config for the SDK and a curl example (see attachment in the thread).

Great questions 2 0
4 quick answers and proposed experiments:

- MRR vs NDCG: MRR improvements suggest the model is promoting a single correct hit higher (good for navigational queries). NDCG@10 being flat can mean the tail ordering beyond the top slot isn't changing much. For CTR correlation, precision@5 and position-weighted CTR (simulated by applying your empirical click model to ranking positions) tend to align better. We can run a small A/B to validate offline correlations.

- top_k tuning: returning top_k=10 and then truncating to top-5 in the UI can help if you have an enrichment/feature augmentation stage that prefers to work on a slightly larger set (e.g., to compute additional signals before final display). But if enrichment is costly and latency-sensitive, prefer top_k=5. For your latency target, start with top_k=10 in staging to measure tail behavior, then drop to 5 for the UI if it meets P95.

- Confidence thresholds: start with a conservative confidence_score >= 0.65 to trigger enrichment; you can lower to 0.5 for recall-heavy flows. We'll help you calibrate with your dataset.

Next steps we propose:
1) Dev to stand up a staging ranking endpoint for Docshelf by EOD Monday.
2) Docshelf runs the sample eval (we'll share a small script to compute MRR/NDCG/precision@k and a position-weighted CTR estimate).
3) Two-week pilot: measure latency and offline metric correlation, then decide UI top_k.

I'll attach the evaluation script and a brief checklist for Dedicated onboarding. Let us know if we should book a quick sync next week to walk through the staging tests.
